'2023-10-04', [1], 'RandomizedDelay_Ephys_Behavior'),\\\\n]\\\\n\\\\nDATA_ROOT = 'data'\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n# ============================================================\\\\n# Smoothing (matches mySmooth.m)\\\\n# ============================================================\\\\ndef causal_gaussian_smooth(x, N, bctype='reflect'):\\\\n    if N <= 1:\\\\n        return x\\\\n    was_1d = (x.ndim == 1)\\\\n    if was_1d:\\\\n        x = x[:, None]\\\\n    if bctype == 'reflect':\\\\n        x_filt = np.concatenate([x[:N, :], x], axis=0)\\\\n        trim = N\\\\n    elif bctype == 'zeropad':\\\\n        x_filt = np.concatenate([np.zeros((N, x.shape[1])), x], axis=0)\\\\n        trim = N\\\\n    else:\\\\n        x_filt = x.copy()\\\\n        trim = 0\\\\n    kern = windows.gaussian(N, std=(N-1)/(2*2.5))\\\\n    kern[:N//2] = 0\\\\n    kern = kern / kern.sum()\\\\n    out = np.zeros_like(x_filt)\\\\n    for j in range(x_filt.shape[1]):\\\\n        out[:, j] = np.convolve(x_filt[:, j], kern, mode='same')\\\\n    out = out[trim:, :]\\\\n    if was_1d:\\\\n        out = out[:, 0]\\\\n    return out\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n# ============================================================\\\\n# Unified data loader (handles both v7.3 HDF5 and v5 MAT)\\\\n# ============================================================\\\\nclass SessionData:\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Unified interface for loading session data from .mat files.\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\n    def __init__(self, fpath):\\\\n        self.fpath = fpath\\\\n        self.is_h5 = self._check_h5(fpath)\\\\n        if self.is_h5:\\\\n            self.f = h5py.File(fpath, 'r')\\\\n            self.obj = self.f['obj']\\\\n        else:\\\\n            mat = sio.loadmat(fpath, squeeze_me=True, struct_as_record=False)\\\\n            self.obj_v5 = mat['obj']\\\\n            self.f = None\\\\n\\\\n    def _check_h5(self, fpath):\\\\n        with open(fpath, 'rb') as ff:\\\\n            header = ff.read(30).decode('ascii', errors='replace')\\\\n        return '7.3' in header\\\\n\\\\n    def close(self):\\\\n        if self.f is not None:\\\\n            self.f.close()\\\\n\\\\n    # --- Trial info ---\\\\n    def get_ntrials(self):\\\\n        if self.is_h5:\\\\n            return int(np.array(self.obj['bp']['Ntrials']).flatten()[0])\\\\n        return int(self.obj_v5.bp.Ntrials)\\\\n\\\\n    def get_trial_array(self, field):\\\\n        \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Get a boolean/numeric trial array from bp (hit, miss, no, R, L, early, autowater).\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n        if self.is_h5:\\\\n            return np.array(self.obj['bp'][field]).flatten()\\\\n        return np.array(getattr(self.obj_v5.bp, field)).flatten()\\\\n\\\\n    def get_stim_enable(self):\\\\n        if self.is_h5:\\\\n            return np.array(self.obj['bp']['stim']['enable']).flatten()\\\\n        return np.array(self.obj_v5.bp.stim.enable).flatten()\\\\n\\\\n    def get_event_times(self, event):\\\\n        if self.is_h5:\\\\n            return np.array(self.obj['bp']['ev'][event]).flatten()\\\\n        return np.array(getattr(self.obj_v5.bp.ev, event)).flatten()\\\\n\\\\n    # --- Cluster data ---\\\\n    def get_clusters(self, probe_nums):\\\\n        \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Get list of (quality, trial_array, trialtm_array) for each cluster.\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n        clusters = []\\\\n        if self.is_h5:\\\\n            clu_ref = self.obj['clu']\\\\n            for pnum in probe_nums:\\\\n                pidx = pnum - 1\\\\n                try:\\\\n                    ref = clu_ref[pidx, 0]\\\\n                    clu_group = self.f[ref]\\\\n                    if not isinstance(clu_group, h5py.Group):\\\\n                        continue\\\\n                except:\\\\n                    continue\\\\n                quality_refs = clu_group['quality']\\\\n                n_clu = quality_refs.shape[0]\\\\n                for i in range(n_clu):\\\\n                    q_ref = quality_refs[i, 0]\\\\n                    val = self.f[q_ref]\\\\n                    q = ''.join(chr(int(c)) for c in np.array(val).flatten()).strip().lower()\\\\n\\\\n                    t_ref = clu_group['trial'][i, 0]\\\\n                    trial = np.array(self.f[t_ref]).flatten()\\\\n\\\\n                    tt_ref = clu_group['trialtm'][i, 0]\\\\n                    trialtm = np.array(self.f[tt_ref]).flatten()\\\\n\\\\n                    clusters.append((q, trial, trialtm))\\\\n        else:\\\\n            clu = self.obj_v5.clu\\\\n            # v5 format: clu is flat array of cluster structs (single probe)\\\\n            # or sometimes cell array {probe1_clusters, probe2_clusters}\\\\n            if isinstance(clu, np.ndarray) and len(clu) > 0:\\\\n                first = clu[0]\\\\n                if hasattr(first, 'quality'):\\\\n                    # Flat array of cluster structs (single probe)\\\\n                    for c in clu:\\\\n                        q = str(c.quality).strip().lower()\\\\n                        trial = np.array(c.trial).flatten()\\\\n                        trialtm = np.array(c.trialtm).flatten()\\\\n                        clusters.append((q, trial, trialtm))\\\\n                elif isinstance(first, np.ndarray):\\\\n                    # Cell array by probe\\\\n                    for pnum in probe_nums:\\\\n                        pidx = pnum - 1\\\\n                        if pidx < len(clu):\\\\n                            probe_clu = clu[pidx]\\\\n                            if isinstance(probe_clu, np.ndarray):\\\\n                                for c in probe_clu:\\\\n                                    q = str(c.quality).strip().lower()\\\\n                                    trial = np.array(c.trial).flatten()\\\\n                                    trialtm = np.array(c.trialtm).flatten()\\\\n                                    clusters.append((q, trial, trialtm))\\\\n        return clusters\\\\n\\\\n    # --- Video offset ---\\\\n    def get_video_offset(self):\\\\n        if self.is_h5:\\\\n            bitStart = np.array(self.obj['bp']['ev']['bitStart']).flatten()\\\\n            sglx_bitstart = np.array(self.obj['sglx']['bitcode']['bitstart']).flatten()\\\\n            sglx_fs = float(np.array(self.obj['sglx']['fs']).flatten()[0])\\\\n        else:\\\\n            bitStart = np.array(self.obj_v5.bp.ev.bitStart).flatten()\\\\n            sglx_bitstart = np.array(self.obj_v5.sglx.bitcode.bitstart).flatten()\\\\n            sglx_fs = float(np.array(self.obj_v5.sglx.fs).flatten()[0])\\\\n\\\\n        bs_mode = float(stats.mode(bitStart, keepdims=False).mode)\\\\n        sglx_mode = float(stats.mode(sglx_bitstart, keepdims=False).mode)\\\\n        return sglx_mode / sglx_fs - bs_mode\\\\n\\\\n    # --- Trajectory data ---\\\\n    def get_traj_feature_names(self, view):\\\\n        \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Get feature names for a camera view (0=side, 1=bottom).\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n        if self.is_h5:\\\\n            traj_ref = self.obj['traj'][view, 0]\\\\n            traj_g = self.f[traj_ref]\\\\n            feat_ref = traj_g['featNames'][0, 0]\\\\n            feat_data = self.f[feat_ref]\\\\n            names = []\\\\n            if feat_data.shape[0] == 1:\\\\n                for i in range(feat_data.shape[1]):\\\\n                    ref = feat_data[0, i]\\\\n                    val = self.f[ref]\\\\n                    names.append(''.join(chr(int(c)) for c in np.array(val).flatten()))\\\\n            else:\\\\n                for i in range(feat_data.shape[0]):\\\\n                    ref = feat_data[i, 0]\\\\n                    val = self.f[ref]\\\\n                    names.append(''.join(chr(int(c)) for c in np.array(val).flatten()))\\\\n            return names\\\\n        else:\\\\n            traj_view = self.obj_v5.traj[view]\\\\n            feats = traj_view[0].featNames\\\\n            if isinstance(feats, str):\\\\n                return [feats]\\\\n            return list(feats)\\\\n\\\\n    def get_trial_traj(self, view, trial_idx, feat_idx):\\\\n        \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Get (frame_times, x, y) for a specific trial and feature.\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n        if self.is_h5:\\\\n            traj_ref = self.obj['traj'][view, 0]\\\\n            traj_g = self.f[traj_ref]\\\\n\\\\n            ft_ref = traj_g['frameTimes'][trial_idx, 0]\\\\n            frame_times = np.array(self.f[ft_ref]).flatten()\\\\n\\\\n            ts_ref = traj_g['ts'][trial_idx, 0]\\\\n            ts = np.array(self.f[ts_ref])\\\\n            # HDF5: (n_feats, 3, n_frames)\\\\n            x = ts[feat_idx, 0, :]\\\\n            y = ts[feat_idx, 1, :]\\\\n        else:\\\\n            traj_view = self.obj_v5.traj[view]\\\\n            trial_data = traj_view[trial_idx]\\\\n            frame_times = np.array(trial_data.frameTimes).flatten()\\\\n            ts = np.array(trial_data.ts)\\\\n            # v5: (n_frames, 3, n_feats)\\\\n            x = ts[:, 0, feat_idx]\\\\n            y = ts[:, 1, feat_idx]\\\\n        return frame_times, x, y\\\\n\\\\n    def get_trial_frame_times(self, view, trial_idx):\\\\n        \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Get frame times for a trial.\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n        if self.is_h5:\\\\n            traj_ref = self.obj['traj'][view, 0]\\\\n            traj_g = self.f[traj_ref]\\\\n            ft_ref = traj_g['frameTimes'][trial_idx, 0]\\\\n            return np.array(self.f[ft_ref]).flatten()\\\\n        else:\\\\n            return np.array(self.obj_v5.traj[view][trial_idx].frameTimes).flatten()\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef load_motion_energy(data_dir, anm, date):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Load motion energy data from .mat file.\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    me_fn = f'motionEnergy_{anm}_{date}.mat'\\\\n    me_path = os.path.join(DATA_ROOT, data_dir, me_fn)\\\\n\\\\n    if not os.path.exists(me_path):\\\\n        return None, None\\\\n\\\\n    try:\\\\n        me_mat = sio.loadmat(me_path, squeeze_me=False, struct_as_record=True)\\\\n        me = me_mat['me'][0, 0]\\\\n        thresh = float(me['moveThresh'].flatten()[0])\\\\n        data_field = me['data']\\\\n        if data_field.dtype.names is not None and 'data' in data_field.dtype.names:\\\\n            data_field = data_field[0, 0]['data']\\\\n        data_arr = data_field.flatten()\\\\n        me_list = [data_arr[i].flatten().astype(float) for i in range(len(data_arr))]\\\\n        return me_list, thresh\\\\n    except Exception as e:\\\\n        try:\\\\n            me_f = h5py.File(me_path, 'r')\\\\n            me = me_f['me']\\\\n            thresh = float(np.array(me['moveThresh']).flatten()[0])\\\\n            data_refs = me['data']\\\\n            me_list = []\\\\n            for i in range(data_refs.shape[0]):\\\\n                ref = data_refs[i, 0]\\\\n                d = np.array(me_f[ref]).flatten()\\\\n                me_list.append(d)\\\\n            me_f.close()\\\\n            return me_list, thresh\\\\n        except Exception as e2:\\\\n            print(f'  WARNING: Cannot load motion energy: {e2}')\\\\n            return None, None\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n# ============================================================\\\\n# Main processing\\\\n# ============================================================\\\\ndef process_session(anm, date, probe_nums, data_dir, time_edges, time_axis):\\\\n    fn = f'data_structure_{anm}_{date}.mat'\\\\n    fpath = os.path.join(DATA_ROOT, data_dir, fn)\\\\n\\\\n    if not os.path.exists(fpath):\\\\n        print(f'  WARNING: File not found: {fpath}')\\\\n        return None\\\\n\\\\n    print(f'  Loading {anm}_{date} (probes {probe_nums})...')\\\\n\\\\n    sd = SessionData(fpath)\\\\n    ntrials = sd.get_ntrials()\\\\n    n_timebins = len(time_axis)\\\\n\\\\n    # Trial info\\\\n    hit = sd.get_trial_array('hit').astype(bool)\\\\n    miss = sd.get_trial_array('miss').astype(bool)\\\\n    R = sd.get_trial_array('R').astype(bool)\\\\n    L = sd.get_trial_array('L').astype(bool)\\\\n    autowater = sd.get_trial_array('autowater')\\\\n    early = sd.get_trial_array('early').astype(bool)\\\\n    stim_enable = sd.get_stim_enable().astype(bool)\\\\n    gocue = sd.get_event_times('goCue')\\\\n\\\\n    # Trial selection: hit or miss, no stim, no early\\\\n    valid_trials = (hit | miss) & ~stim_enable & ~early\\\\n    valid_idx = np.where(valid_trials)[0]\\\\n\\\\n    if len(valid_idx) < 5:\\\\n        print(f'  WARNING: Too few valid trials ({len(valid_idx)}), skipping')\\\\n        sd.close()\\\\n        return None\\\\n\\\\n    # Get clusters\\\\n    clusters = sd.get_clusters(probe_nums)\\\\n    # Filter by quality\\\\n    filtered_clusters = [(q, t, tt) for q, t, tt in clusters if q not in EXCLUDE_QUALITIES]\\\\n\\\\n    if len(filtered_clusters) == 0:\\\\n        print(f'  WARNING: No valid clusters, skipping')\\\\n        sd.close()\\\\n        return None\\\\n\\\\n    n_units = len(filtered_clusters)\\\\n\\\\n    # Bin spikes aligned to go cue\\\\n    trialdat = np.zeros((n_units, n_timebins, ntrials))\\\\n    for i, (q, trial_nums, spike_times) in enumerate(filtered_clusters):\\\\n        for j in range(ntrials):\\\\n            trial_mask = (trial_nums == (j + 1))\\\\n            if not np.any(trial_mask):\\\\n                continue\\\\n            aligned_times = spike_times[trial_mask] - gocue[j]\\\\n            counts, _ = np.histogram(aligned_times, bins=time_edges)\\\\n            fr = counts / DT\\\\n            trialdat[i, :, j] = causal_gaussian_smooth(fr, SMOOTH_WINDOW, BC_TYPE)\\\\n\\\\n    # Remove low FR units\\\\n    mean_frs = np.mean(np.mean(trialdat[:, :, valid_idx], axis=2), axis=1)\\\\n    keep_units = mean_frs > LOW_FR_THRESH\\\\n\\\\n    if keep_units.sum() < 10:\\\\n        print(f'  WARNING: Only {keep_units.sum()} units with FR>{LOW_FR_THRESH} Hz, skipping')\\\\n        sd.close()\\\\n        return None\\\\n\\\\n    trialdat = trialdat[keep_units, :, :]\\\\n    n_units_final = trialdat.shape[0]\\\\n    print(f'  {n_units_final} units after filtering (from {n_units} total)')\\\\n\\\\n    # Video offset\\\\n    vidshift = sd.get_video_offset()\\\\n\\\\n    # Get feature indices for tongue and paw (bottom cam)\\\\n    try:\\\\n        bottom_feats = sd.get_traj_feature_names(1)\\\\n        tongue_feat_idx = None\\\\n        paw_feat_idx = None\\\\n        for idx, name in enumerate(bottom_feats):\\\\n            if name == 'top_tongue' and tongue_feat_idx is None:\\\\n                tongue_feat_idx = idx\\\\n            if name == 'bottom_paw' and paw_feat_idx is None:\\\\n                paw_feat_idx = idx\\\\n        if tongue_feat_idx is None:\\\\n            for idx, name in enumerate(bottom_feats):\\\\n                if 'tongue' in name.lower():\\\\n                    tongue_feat_idx = idx\\\\n                    break\\\\n        if paw_feat_idx is None:\\\\n            for idx, name in enumerate(bottom_feats):\\\\n                if 'paw' in name.lower():\\\\n                    paw_feat_idx = idx\\\\n                    break\\\\n    except:\\\\n        tongue_feat_idx = None\\\\n        paw_feat_idx = None\\\\n\\\\n    # Load motion energy\\\\n    me_data, me_thresh = load_motion_energy(data_dir, anm, date)\\\\n\\\\n    # Process each valid trial\\\\n    neural_trials = []\\\\n    input_trials = []\\\\n    raw_outputs = []\\\\n\\\\n    for trial_idx in valid_idx:\\\\n        neural = trialdat[:, :, trial_idx]\\\\n        input_data = time_axis.reshape(1, -1).copy()\\\\n\\\\n        lick_dir = 1 if R[trial_idx] else 0\\\\n        context = 0 if autowater[trial_idx] == 1 else 1\\\\n        outcome = 1 if hit[trial_idx] else 0\\\\n\\\\n        # Tongue velocity\\\\n        tongue_vel = np.full(n_timebins, np.nan)\\\\n        if tongue_feat_idx is not None:\\\\n            try:\\\\n                ft, x, y = sd.get_trial_traj(1, trial_idx, tongue_feat_idx)\\\\n                dt_vid = 1.0 / VIDEO_FPS\\\\n                vel = np.sqrt(np.diff(x)**2 + np.diff(y)**2) / dt_vid\\\\n                vel_t = ft[:-1] + dt_vid / 2\\\\n                vel_t_aligned = vel_t - vidshift - gocue[trial_idx]\\\\n                tongue_vel = np.interp(time_axis, vel_t_aligned, vel, left=np.nan, right=np.nan)\\\\n            except:\\\\n                pass\\\\n\\\\n        # Paw velocity\\\\n        paw_vel = np.full(n_timebins, np.nan)\\\\n        if paw_feat_idx is not None:\\\\n            try:\\\\n                ft, x, y = sd.get_trial_traj(1, trial_idx, paw_feat_idx)\\\\n                dt_vid = 1.0 / VIDEO_FPS\\\\n                vel = np.sqrt(np.diff(x)**2 + np.diff(y)**2) / dt_vid\\\\n                vel_t = ft[:-1] + dt_vid / 2\\\\n                vel_t_aligned = vel_t - vidshift - gocue[trial_idx]\\\\n                paw_vel = np.interp(time_axis, vel_t_aligned, vel, left=np.nan, right=np.nan)\\\\n            except:\\\\n                pass\\\\n\\\\n        # Motion energy\\\\n        me_interp = np.full(n_timebins, np.nan)\\\\n        if me_data is not None and trial_idx < len(me_data):\\\\n            try:\\\\n                ft = sd.get_trial_frame_times(1, trial_idx)\\\\n                ft_aligned = ft - vidshift - gocue[trial_idx]\\\\n                me_interp = np.interp(time_axis, ft_aligned, me_data[trial_idx], left=np.nan, right=np.nan)\\\\n            except:\\\\n                pass\\\\n\\\\n        neural_trials.append(neural)\\\\n        input_trials.append(input_data)\\\\n        raw_outputs.append({\\\\n            'lick_dir': lick_dir,\\\\n            'context': context,\\\\n            'outcome': outcome,\\\\n            'tongue_vel': tongue_vel,\\\\n            'paw_vel': paw_vel,\\\\n            'motion_energy': me_interp,\\\\n        })\\\\n\\\\n    sd.close()\\\\n\\\\n    if len(neural_trials) < 2:\\\\n        print(f'  WARNING: Only {len(neural_trials)} valid trials, skipping')\\\\n        return None\\\\n\\\\n    # Discretize continuous outputs per session (50th percentile threshold)\\\\n    all_tongue = np.concatenate([t['tongue_vel'] for t in raw_outputs])\\\\n    all_paw = np.concatenate([t['paw_vel'] for t in raw_outputs])\\\\n    all_me = np.concatenate([t['motion_energy'] for t in raw_outputs])\\\\n\\\\n    tongue_thresh = np.nanpercentile(all_tongue, 50) if not np.all(np.isnan(all_tongue)) else 0\\\\n    paw_thresh = np.nanpercentile(all_paw, 50) if not np.all(np.isnan(all_paw)) else 0\\\\n    me_thresh_50 = np.nanpercentile(all_me, 50) if not np.all(np.isnan(all_me)) else 0\\\\n\\\\n    final_output_trials = []\\\\n    for t in raw_outputs:\\\\n        tongue_disc = np.where(np.isnan(t['tongue_vel']), 0,\\\\n                              np.where(t['tongue_vel'] >= tongue_thresh, 1, 0)).astype(np.int64)\\\\n        paw_disc = np.where(np.isnan(t['paw_vel']), 0,\\\\n                           np.where(t['paw_vel'] >= paw_thresh, 1, 0)).astype(np.int64)\\\\n        me_disc = np.where(np.isnan(t['motion_energy']), 0,\\\\n                          np.where(t['motion_energy'] >= me_thresh_50, 1, 0)).astype(np.int64)\\\\n\\\\n        out = np.zeros((6, n_timebins), dtype=np.int64)\\\\n        out[0, :] = t['lick_dir']\\\\n        out[1, :] = t['context']\\\\n        out[2, :] = t['outcome']\\\\n        out[3, :] = tongue_disc\\\\n        out[4, :] = paw_disc\\\\n        out[5, :] = me_disc\\\\n        final_output_trials.append(out)\\\\n\\\\n    return {\\\\n        'neural': neural_trials,\\\\n        'input': input_trials,\\\\n        'output': final_output_trials,\\\\n        'n_units': ============================================================\\\\n# Helper functions\\\\n# ============================================================\\\\n\\\\ndef causal_gaussian_smooth(x, N, bctype='reflect'):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    Causal Gaussian smoothing matching mySmooth.m.\\\\n    x: (n_timepoints,) or (n_timepoints, n_cols)\\\\n    N: window size\\\\n    bctype: 'reflect', 'zeropad', or 'none'\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    if N <= 1:\\\\n        return x\\\\n\\\\n    was_1d = (x.ndim == 1)\\\\n    if was_1d:\\\\n        x = x[:, None]\\\\n\\\\n video/\\n# These are the sessions with electrophysiology + video\\n# We include both Ephys_Behavior (two-context + DR-only) and RandomizedDelay sessions\\n\\nEPHYS_SESSIONS = [\\n    # Two-context paradigm sessions (Ephys_Behavior)\\n    ('EKH1', '2021-08-07', [2], 'Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('EKH3', '2021-08-11', [2], 'Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB6', '2021-04-18', [2], 'Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB7', '2021-04-29', [1], 'Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB7', '2021-04-30', [1], 'Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JGR2', '2021-11-16', [1], 'Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JGR2', '2021-11-17', [1], '2022-07-26', [1, 2], 'Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB15', '2022-07-27', [1, 2], 'Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB15', '2022-07-28', [1, 2], 'Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB15', '2022-07-29', [2], 'Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB19', '2023-04-18', [1], 'Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB19', '2023-04-19', [1], 'Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB19', '2023-04-20', [1], 'Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB19', '2023-04-21', [1], 'Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    # Randomized delay sessions\\n    ('JEB11', '2022-05-10', [1], 'RandomizedDelay_Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB11', '2022-05-11', [1], 'RandomizedDelay_Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB12', '2022-05-12', [1], 'RandomizedDelay_Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB12', '2022-05-13', [1], 'RandomizedDelay_Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB23', '2023-10-10', [1], 'RandomizedDelay_Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB23', '2023-10-11', [1], 'RandomizedDelay_Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB23', '2023-10-12', [1], 'RandomizedDelay_Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB23', '2023-10-13', [1], 'RandomizedDelay_Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB23', '2023-10-18', [1], 'RandomizedDelay_Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB23', '2023-10-19', [1], 'RandomizedDelay_Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB23', '2023-10-21', [1], 'RandomizedDelay_Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB24', '2023-10-23', [1], 'RandomizedDelay_Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB24', '2023-10-24', [1], 'RandomizedDelay_Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB24', '2023-10-25', [1], 'RandomizedDelay_Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB24', '2023-10-26', [1], 'RandomizedDelay_Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB24', '2023-10-27', [1], 'RandomizedDelay_Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB24', '2023-10-31', [1], 'RandomizedDelay_Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB24', '2023-11-02', [1], 'RandomizedDelay_Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB24', '2023-11-03', [1], 'RandomizedDelay_Ephys_Behavior'),\\n    ('JEB23', '2023-10-20', [1], 'RandomizedDelay_Ephys_Behavior'),\\n]\\n\\nDATA_ROOT = 'data'\\n\\n\\n# ============================================================\\n# Helper functions\\n# ============================================================\\n\\ndef causal_gaussian_smooth(x, N, bctype='reflect'):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    Causal Gaussian smoothing matching mySmooth.m.\\n    x: (n_timepoints,) or (n_timepoints, n_cols)\\n    N: window size\\n    bctype: 'reflect', 'zeropad', or 'none'\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    if N <= 1:\\n        return x\\n\\n    was_1d = (x.ndim == 1)\\n    if was_1d:\\n        x = x[:, None]\\n\\n    # Boundary condition handling\\n    if bctype == 'reflect':\\n        x_filt = np.concatenate([x[:N, :], x], axis=0)\\n        trim = N\\n    elif bctype == 'zeropad':\\n        x_filt = np.concatenate([np.zeros((N, x.shape[1])), x], axis=0)\\n        trim = N\\n    else:\\n        x_filt = x.copy()\\n        trim = 0\\n\\n    # Gaussian kernel (matching MATLAB gausswin)\\n    kern = windows.gaussian(N, std=(N-1)/(2*2.5))  # MATLAB gausswin default alpha=2.5\\n\\n    # Make causal: zero out first half\\n    kern[:N//2] = 0\\n    kern = kern / kern.sum()\\n\\n    # Convolve\\n    out = np.zeros_like(x_filt)\\n    for j in range(x_filt.shape[1]):\\n        out[:, j] = np.convolve(x_filt[:, j], kern, mode='same')\\n\\n    out = out[trim:, :]\\n\\n    if was_1d:\\n        out = out[:, 0]\\n    return out\\n\\n\\ndef read_h5_string(f, ref):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Read a string from an HDF5 object reference.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    val = f[ref]\\n    chars = np.array(val).flatten()\\n    return ''.join(chr(int(c)) for c in chars)\\n\\n\\ndef get_cluster_qualities(f, clu_group):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Get quality labels for all clusters in a probe's cluster group.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    quality_refs = clu_group['quality']\\n    n_clusters = quality_refs.shape[0]\\n    qualities = []\\n    for i in range(n_clusters):\\n        ref = quality_refs[i, 0]\\n        q = read_h5_string(f, ref)\\n        qualities.append(q.strip().lower())\\n    return qualities\\n\\n\\ndef get_spike_data(f, clu_group, clu_idx):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Get spike trial numbers and trial times for a specific cluster.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    trial_ref = clu_group['trial'][clu_idx, 0]\\n    trial = np.array(f[trial_ref]).flatten()\\n\\n    trialtm_ref = clu_group['trialtm'][clu_idx, 0]\\n    trialtm = np.array(f[trialtm_ref]).flatten()\\n\\n    return trial, trialtm\\n\\n\\ndef compute_video_offset(f, obj):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Compute video offset matching findVideoOffset.m.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    bitStart = np.array(obj['bp']['ev']['bitStart']).flatten()\\n    sglx_bitstart = np.array(obj['sglx']['bitcode']['bitstart']).flatten()\\n    sglx_fs = float(np.array(obj['sglx']['fs']).flatten()[0])\\n\\n    bitStart_mode = float(stats.mode(bitStart, keepdims=False).mode)\\n    sglx_bitstart_mode = float(stats.mode(sglx_bitstart, keepdims=False).mode)\\n\\n    vidshift = sglx_bitstart_mode / sglx_fs - bitStart_mode\\n    return vidshift\\n\\n\\ndef get_traj_feature_names(f, traj_group, trial_idx=0):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Get feature names from trajectory data.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    feat_ref = traj_group['featNames'][trial_idx, 0]\\n    feat_data = f[feat_ref]\\n    names = []\\n    # Could be (1, n_feats) or (n_feats, 1)\\n    if feat_data.shape[0] == 1:\\n        for i in range(feat_data.shape[1]):\\n            ref = feat_data[0, i]\\n            names.append(read_h5_string(f, ref))\\n    else:\\n        for i in range(feat_data.shape[0]):\\n            ref = feat_data[i, 0]\\n            names.append(read_h5_string(f, ref))\\n    return names\\n\\n\\ndef compute_velocity_from_traj(f, traj_group, trial_idx, feat_idx, n_timepoints, gocue_time, vidshift, time_axis):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    Compute velocity of a tracked feature for a trial, interpolated to time_axis.\\n    Returns velocity as a 1D array aligned to time_axis.\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    # Get frame times\\n    ft_ref = traj_group['frameTimes'][trial_idx, 0]\\n    frame_times = np.array(f[ft_ref]).flatten()\\n\\n    # Get tracking data: shape (n_features, 3, n_frames) where 3=[x,y,conf]\\n    ts_ref = traj_group['ts'][trial_idx, 0]\\n    ts = np.array(f[ts_ref])\\n\\n    # ts shape from HDF5 is (n_feats, 3, n_frames)\\n    x = ts[feat_idx, 0, :]  # x coordinate\\n    y = ts[feat_idx, 1, :]  # y coordinate\\n\\n    # Fill missing values with nearest (matching methods: \\\"Missing values were filled in\\n    # with the nearest available value for all features, except for the tongue\\\")\\n    # For tongue, we don't fill - but for velocity calculation we need to handle NaNs\\n\\n    # Compute velocity as first-order derivative\\n    # Velocity = sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2) / dt\\n    dt_vid = 1.0 / VIDEO_FPS\\n    dx = np.diff(x)\\n    dy = np.diff(y)\\n    vel = np.sqrt(dx**2 + dy**2) / dt_vid\\n    vel_times = frame_times[:-1] + dt_vid / 2  # midpoint times\\n\\n    # Align to go cue: subtract vidshift and gocue_time\\n    vel_times_aligned = vel_times - vidshift - gocue_time\\n\\n    # Interpolate to time_axis\\n    try:\\n        vel_interp = np.interp(time_axis, vel_times_aligned, vel, left=np.nan, right=np.nan)\\n    except:\\n        vel_interp = np.full(len(time_axis), np.nan)\\n\\n    return vel_interp\\n\\n\\ndef load_motion_energy(data_dir, anm, date):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Load motion energy data from .mat file.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    me_fn = f'motionEnergy_{anm}_{date}.mat'\\n    me_path = os.path.join(DATA_ROOT, data_dir, me_fn)\\n\\n    if not os.path.exists(me_path):\\n        return None, None\\n\\n    try:\\n        me_mat = sio.loadmat(me_path, squeeze_me=False, struct_as_record=True)\\n        me = me_mat['me'][0, 0]\\n        thresh = float(me['moveThresh'].flatten()[0])\\n        data_field = me['data']\\n        # Handle nested struct: if me.data is itself a struct with 'data' field\\n        # (matching loadMotionEnergy.m: if isstruct(me.data); me.data = me.data.data; end)\\n        if data_field.dtype.names is not None and 'data' in data_field.dtype.names:\\n            data_field = data_field[0, 0]['data']\\n        data_arr = data_field.flatten()\\n        me_list = [data_arr[i].flatten().astype(float) for i in range(len(data_arr))]\\n        return me_list, thresh\\n    except:\\n        try:\\n            me_f = h5py.File(me_path, 'r')\\n            me = me_f['me']\\n            thresh = float(np.array(me['moveThresh']).flatten()[0])\\n            data_refs = me['data']\\n            me_data = []\\n            for i in range(data_refs.shape[0]):\\n                ref = data_refs[i, 0]\\n                d = np.array(me_f[ref]).flatten()\\n                me_data.append(d)\\n            me_f.close()\\n            return me_data, thresh\\n        except:\\n            return None, None\\n\\n\\ndef interpolate_me_to_time_axis(me_trial, frame_times, vidshift, gocue_time, time_axis):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Interpolate motion energy to time_axis, aligned to go cue.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    ft_aligned = frame_times - vidshift - gocue_time\\n    try:\\n        me_interp = np.interp(time_axis, ft_aligned, me_trial, left=np.nan, right=np.nan)\\n    except:\\n        me_interp = np.full(len(time_axis), np.nan)\\n    return me_interp\\n\\n\\n# ============================================================\\n# Main processing\\n# ============================================================\\n\\ndef process_session(anm, date, probe_nums, data_dir, time_edges, time_axis):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    Process a single session. Returns dict with neural, input, output data per trial,\\n    or None if session doesn't meet criteria.\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    fn = f'data_structure_{anm}_{date}.mat'\\n    fpath = os.path.join(DATA_ROOT, data_dir, fn)\\n\\n    if not os.path.exists(fpath):\\n        print(f'  WARNING: File not found: {fpath}')\\n        return None\\n\\n    print(f'  Loading {anm}_{date} (probes {probe_nums})...')\\n\\n    f = h5py.File(fpath, 'r')\\n    obj = f['obj']\\n    bp = obj['bp']\\n\\n    # === Extract trial info ===\\n    ntrials = int(np.array(bp['Ntrials']).flatten()[0])\\n    hit = np.array(bp['hit']).flatten().astype(bool)\\n    miss = np.array(bp['miss']).flatten().astype(bool)\\n    no = np.array(bp['no']).flatten().astype(bool)\\n    R = np.array(bp['R']).flatten().astype(bool)\\n    L = np.array(bp['L']).flatten().astype(bool)\\n    autowater = np.array(bp['autowater']).flatten()\\n    early = np.array(bp['early']).flatten().astype(bool)\\n    stim_enable = np.array(bp['stim']['enable']).flatten().astype(bool)\\n\\n    gocue = np.array(bp['ev']['goCue']).flatten()\\n\\n    # === Trial selection (matching reference code conditions) ===\\n    # Include: hit or miss trials, no stim, no early lick\\n    # Exclude: ignore trials (no response), stim trials, early lick trials\\n    # Conditions from code:\\n    #   'R&hit&~stim.enable&~autowater&~early'  -> right correct DR\\n    #   'L&hit&~stim.enable&~autowater&~early'  -> left correct DR\\n    #   'R&miss&~stim.enable&~autowater&~early' -> right error DR\\n    #   'L&miss&~stim.enable&~autowater&~early' -> left error DR\\n    #   'R&hit&~stim.enable&autowater&~early'   -> right correct WC\\n    #   'L&hit&~stim.enable&autowater&~early'   -> left correct WC\\n    # We include all hit and miss trials (not ignore/no), excluding stim and early\\n    valid_trials = (hit | miss) & ~stim_enable & ~early\\n    valid_idx = np.where(valid_trials)[0]\\n\\n    if len(valid_idx) < 5:\\n        print(f'  WARNING: Too few valid trials ({len(valid_idx)}), skipping')\\n        f.close()\\n        return None\\n\\n    # === Extract cluster data from specified probes ===\\n    clu_ref = obj['clu']\\n    all_spike_trials = []\\n    all_spike_trialtm = []\\n    all_qualities = []\\n\\n    for probe_num in probe_nums:\\n        probe_idx = probe_num - 1  # 0-indexed\\n        try:\\n            ref = clu_ref[probe_idx, 0]\\n            clu_group = f[ref]\\n            if not isinstance(clu_group, h5py.Group):\\n                print(f'  WARNING: Probe {probe_num} has no cluster data, skipping probe')\\n                continue\\n        except:\\n            print(f'  WARNING: Cannot access probe {probe_num}, skipping probe')\\n            continue\\n\\n        qualities = get_cluster_qualities(f, clu_group)\\n        n_clu = len(qualities)\\n\\n        for i in range(n_clu):\\n            q = qualities[i]\\n            if q in EXCLUDE_QUALITIES:\\n                continue\\n            trial, trialtm = get_spike_data(f, clu_group, i)\\n            all_spike_trials.append(trial)\\n            all_spike_trialtm.append(trialtm)\\n            all_qualities.append(q)\\n\\n    if len(all_spike_trials) == 0:\\n        print(f'  WARNING: No valid clusters found, skipping')\\n        f.close()\\n        return None\\n\\n    n_units = len(all_spike_trials)\\n\\n    # === Align spikes to go cue and bin ===\\n    n_timebins = len(time_axis)\\n\\n    # Single trial firing rates: (n_units, n_timebins, n_trials)\\n    trialdat = np.zeros((n_units, n_timebins, ntrials))\\n\\n    for i in range(n_units):\\n        trial_nums = all_spike_trials[i]\\n        spike_times = all_spike_trialtm[i]\\n\\n        for j in range(ntrials):\\n            trial_mask = (trial_nums == (j + 1))  # trials are 1-indexed in MATLAB\\n            if not np.any(trial_mask):\\n                continue\\n\\n            spk_times = spike_times[trial_mask]\\n            # Align to go cue\\n            aligned_times = spk_times - gocue[j]\\n\\n            # Bin spikes\\n            counts, _ = np.histogram(aligned_times, bins=time_edges)\\n            # Convert to firing rate and smooth\\n            fr = counts / DT\\n            fr_smooth = causal_gaussian_smooth(fr, SMOOTH_WINDOW, BC_TYPE)\\n            trialdat[i, :, j] = fr_smooth\\n\\n    # === Remove low firing rate units ===\\n    # Mean FR across all time bins and all trials (matching removeLowFRClusters.m)\\n    # The reference computes mean of the PSTH (trial-averaged), but we approximate\\n    # by computing mean across all time and trials\\n    mean_frs = np.mean(np.mean(trialdat[:, :, valid_idx], axis=2), axis=1)\\n    keep_units = mean_frs > LOW_FR_THRESH\\n\\n    if keep_units.sum() < 10:\\n        print(f'  WARNING: Only {keep_units.sum()} units with FR > {LOW_FR_THRESH} Hz (need >= 10), skipping')\\n        f.close()\\n        return None\\n\\n    trialdat = trialdat[keep_units, :, :]\\n    n_units_final = trialdat.shape[0]\\n    print(f'  {n_units_final} units after filtering (from {n_units} total)')\\n\\n    # === Compute video offset ===\\n    vidshift = compute_video_offset(f, obj)\\n\\n    # === Load trajectory data for tongue and paw velocity ===\\n    traj_ref = obj['traj']\\n\\n    # Bottom cam for tongue and paw\\n    bottom_ref = traj_ref[1, 0]\\n    bottom_traj = f[bottom_ref]\\n    bottom_feats = get_traj_feature_names(f, bottom_traj, 0)\\n    # Find tongue feature index (top_tongue) and paw feature index (top_paw or bottom_paw)\\n    tongue_feat_idx = None\\n    paw_feat_idx = None\\n    for idx, name in enumerate(bottom_feats):\\n        if name == 'top_tongue':\\n            tongue_feat_idx = idx\\n        if name == 'bottom_paw':\\n            paw_feat_idx = idx\\n    if tongue_feat_idx is None:\\n        # Fall back to any tongue feature\\n        for idx, name in enumerate(bottom_feats):\\n            if 'tongue' in name.lower():\\n                tongue_feat_idx = idx\\n                break\\n    if paw_feat_idx is None:\\n        for idx, name in enumerate(bottom_feats):\\n            if 'paw' in name.lower():\\n                paw_feat_idx = idx\\n                break\\n\\n    # === Load motion energy ===\\n    me_data, me_thresh = load_motion_energy(data_dir, anm, date)\\n\\n    # === Process each valid trial ===\\n    neural_trials = []\\n    input_trials = []\\n    output_trials = []\\n    trial_indices_used = []\\n\\n    for trial_idx in valid_idx:\\n        # Neural data for this trial\\n        neural = trialdat[:, :, trial_idx]  # (n_units, n_timebins)\\n\\n        # Input: time from go cue (same for all trials)\\n        input_data = time_axis.reshape(1, -1).copy()  # (1, n_timebins)\\n\\n        # === Output variables ===\\n        # Lick direction: left=0, right=1\\n        lick_dir = 1 if R[trial_idx] else 0\\n\\n        # Behavioral context: WC=0, DR=1\\n        context = 0 if autowater[trial_idx] == 1 else 1\\n\\n        # Outcome: incorrect=0, correct=1\\n        outcome = 1 if hit[trial_idx] else 0\\n\\n        # Tongue velocity (time-varying)\\n        if tongue_feat_idx is not None:\\n            tongue_vel = compute_velocity_from_traj(\\n                f, bottom_traj, trial_idx, tongue_feat_idx,\\n                n_timebins, gocue[trial_idx], vidshift, time_axis\\n            )\\n        else:\\n            tongue_vel = np.full(n_timebins, np.nan)\\n\\n        # Paw velocity (time-varying)\\n        if paw_feat_idx is not None:\\n            paw_vel = compute_velocity_from_traj(\\n                f, bottom_traj, trial_idx, paw_feat_idx,\\n                n_timebins, gocue[trial_idx], vidshift, time_axis\\n            )\\n        else:\\n            paw_vel = np.full(n_timebins, np.nan)\\n\\n        # Motion energy (time-varying)\\n        if me_data is not None:\\n            # Get frame times for this trial\\n            ft_ref = bottom_traj['frameTimes'][trial_idx, 0]\\n            frame_times = np.array(f[ft_ref]).flatten()\\n            me_trial = me_data[trial_idx]\\n            me_interp = interpolate_me_to_time_axis(\\n                me_trial, frame_times, vidshift, gocue[trial_idx], time_axis\\n            )\\n        else:\\n            me_interp = np.full(n_timebins, np.nan)\\n\\n        neural_trials.append(neural)\\n        input_trials.append(input_data)\\n\\n        # Store raw continuous values; discretization happens per-session after all trials\\n        output_trials.append({\\n            'lick_dir': lick_dir,\\n            'context': context,\\n            'outcome': outcome,\\n            'tongue_vel': tongue_vel,\\n            'paw_vel': paw_vel,\\n            'motion_energy': me_interp,\\n        })\\n        trial_indices_used.append(trial_idx)\\n\\n    f.close()\\n\\n    if len(neural_trials) < 2:\\n        print(f'  WARNING: Only {len(neural_trials)} valid trials, need at least 2, skipping')\\n        return None\\n\\n    # === Discretize continuous outputs per session ===\\n    # Collect all tongue_vel, paw_vel, motion_energy across trials for percentile\\n    all_tongue = np.concatenate([t['tongue_vel'] for t in output_trials])\\n    all_paw = np.concatenate([t['paw_vel'] for t in output_trials])\\n    all_me = np.concatenate([t['motion_energy'] for t in output_trials])\\n\\n    # Remove NaNs for percentile computation\\n    tongue_thresh = np.nanpercentile(all_tongue, 50) if not np.all(np.isnan(all_tongue)) else 0\\n    paw_thresh = np.nanpercentile(all_paw, 50) if not np.all(np.isnan(all_paw)) else 0\\n    me_thresh_50 = np.nanpercentile(all_me, 50) if not np.all(np.isnan(all_me)) else 0\\n\\n    # Build final output arrays\\n    final_output_trials = []\\n    for t in output_trials:\\n        tongue_disc = np.where(np.isnan(t['tongue_vel']), 0,\\n                              np.where(t['tongue_vel'] >= tongue_thresh, 1, 0)).astype(np.int64)\\n        paw_disc = np.where(np.isnan(t['paw_vel']), 0,\\n                           np.where(t['paw_vel'] >= paw_thresh, 1, 0)).astype(np.int64)\\n        me_disc = np.where(np.isnan(t['motion_energy']), 0,\\n                          np.where(t['motion_energy'] >= me_thresh_50, 1, 0)).astype(np.int64)\\n\\n        # Output array: (6, n_timebins) for time-varying, or (6,) for per-trial\\n        # lick_dir, context, outcome are per-trial (scalar)\\n        # tongue_vel, paw_vel, motion_energy are time-varying\\n        out = np.zeros((6, n_timebins), dtype=np.int64)\\n        out[0, :] = t['lick_dir']\\n        out[1, :] = t['context']\\n        out[2, :] = t['outcome']\\n        out[3, :] = tongue_disc\\n        out[4, :] = paw_disc\\n        out[5, :] = me_disc\\n\\n        final_output_trials.append(out)\\n\\n    return {\\n        'neural': neural_trials,\\n        'input': input_trials,\\n        'output': final_output_trials,\\n        'n_units': n_units_final,\\n        'anm': anm,\\n        'date': date,\\n        'n_trials': len(neural_trials),\\n        'n_valid_total': len(valid_idx),\\n    }\\n\\n\\ndef main(output_file='converted_data.pkl', sample_file='sample_data.pkl'):\\n    # Time bin edges and centers\\n    time_edges = np.arange(TMIN, TMAX + DT, DT)\\n    time_axis = time_edges[:-1] + DT / 2\\n    n_timebins = len(time_axis)\\n\\n    print(f'Time axis: {n_timebins} bins, {TMIN} to {TMAX} s, dt={DT*1000:.0f} ms')\\n\\n    # In this paradigm, head-fixed mice performed two directional licking tasks that alternated block-wise within each behavioral session. These tasks varied in their cognitive demands but required the same instructed motor output.\\n     4→\\n     5→This paradigm included an established delayed-response (DR) task in which motor planning is temporally dissociated from movement execution (Fig. 1a). In the DR task, an auditory stimulus indicated the location of a reward. After a brief delay epoch with no auditory stimuli, a separate auditory ‘go cue’ instructed the mouse to move. If the mouse performed a directional tongue movement to the correct target, a water reward was delivered. In separate blocks of trials, mice performed a water-cued (WC) task in which all auditory stimuli were omitted. Instead, a drop of water was presented at a random point in time at a randomly selected reward port. Animals consumed water upon its presentation. Mice received no explicit cues signaling DR and WC blocks. The DR task required a perceptual decision that guides the planning of a subsequent motor action. In the WC task, uncertainty in the timing and location of reward prevented formation of a motor plan before reward presentation, and, instead, mice detected reward availability using olfactory and/or vibrissal cues. This structure required animals to maintain an internal representation of the current block identity (context) to maintain high task performance.\\n     6→\\n     7→We examined uninstructed movements in this behavioral paradigm using high-speed video. We tracked movement of the tongue, jaw, nose and paws and calculated instantaneous motion energy to quantify movement in a feature-agnostic manner (Fig. 1d–f). We found that mice performed uninstructed movements that varied in their identity and timing across both trials and contexts (Fig. 1e and Supplementary Movie 1).\\n     8→\\n     9→To assess cortical involvement in instructed movements (directional licking) in both behavioral tasks, we used optogenetic photoinactivation to inhibit the ALM and tjM1 at the go cue (DR) or water presentation (WC) bilaterally in VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice (10 sessions, four mice). Simultaneous photoinactivation of both regions at the go cue (DR task) or water drop (WC task) impaired the initiation of movement in both contexts (Fig. 1b,c; all DR trials: 41 ± 20% reduction, mean ± s.d., P = 1 × 10−4; all WC trials: 15 ± 20%, P = 0.04; and Extended Data Fig. 1c,d). To assess cortical involvement in the expression of uninstructed movements, and whether these movements might be controlled by ALM or tjM1 preferentially, we bilaterally silenced the ALM or tjM1 individually during the delay epoch of DR trials (ALM: 15 sessions, tjM1: nine sessions, four mice). Uninstructed movements were suppressed by photoinactivation of either area (Extended Data Fig. 1b; ALM: 53 ± 31% reduction, mean ± s.d., P = 3 × 10−4; tjM1: 62 ± 24% reduction, P = 2 × 10−3, paired t-test) and more strongly suppressed by concurrent photoinactivation of both areas (Fig. 1g,h; 29 sessions, four mice; 73 ± 35% reduction, mean ± s.d., P = 7 × 10−9, paired t-test), similar to previous observations21 (but see ref. 34). In the DR task, delay photoinactivation of both areas led to a significant decrease in overall performance (Fig. 1i; 22% ± 14% reduction, mean ± s.d., P = 2 × 10−6 paired t-test; Extended Data Fig. 1b) as expected from the disruption of choice/planning dynamics, often leading to animals responding consistently to a preferred side rather than in a manner commensurate with the sensory cue. These results indicate that both the ALM and tjM1 are involved in the generation of uninstructed movements and the planning and execution of instructed directional tongue movements in the two-context paradigm.\\n    10→\\n    11→Neural dynamics related to task variables\\n    12→\\n    13→While movement-related and task-related information is encoded in both the ALM and tjM1 in the DR task and other directional licking tasks33, task variables are more strongly represented in the ALM33,36, and so we focused our subsequent analyses there. We recorded activity extracellularly in the ALM with high-density silicon probes during the two-context paradigm to track dynamics associated with planning, context and the execution of movements (Fig. 2; two-context paradigm: 12 sessions, six mice, 522 units, including 214 well-isolated single units; an additional three mice were trained only on the DR task: 25 sessions, nine mice, 1,651 units, including 483 well-isolated single units; see Extended Data Fig. 2a for per-session statistics). In the DR task, we found that choice selectivity (right versus left DR trials) was widespread across all task epochs as expected (sample: 36%; delay: 42%; response: 58% of 483 single units; 25 sessions, nine mice). Individual units showed a variety of activity patterns across trial types, including delay epoch preparatory activity, which has often been taken to be a neural signature of motor planning32,37 (Fig. 2b, left). Individual units were also selective for behavioral context during all task epochs, including during the inter-trial interval (ITI) (39% of single units, 12 sessions, six mice, 214 single units), suggesting persistent coding of context (Fig. 2b, right).\\n    14→\\n    15→Methods\\n    16→\\n    17→Mouse behavior\\n    18→\\n    19→Behavioral training was conducted using custom scripts written for Bpod r0.5 (https://www.sanworks.io/shop/products.php?productFamily=bpod). All mice used in experiments were first trained on the DR task with a fixed delay epoch until they reached at least 70% accuracy. At the beginning of each trial, one of two auditory tones lasting 1.3 s was played; the tone indicating a ‘right’ trial was white noise, and the tone indicating a ‘left’ trial was a pure tone (8-kHz pulses). The delay epoch (0.9 s for 12 mice, 0.7 s for one mouse and linearly time warped to 0.9 s) started after the completion of the sample tone. After the delay epoch, an auditory go cue was played (swept-frequency cosine (chirp), 10 ms), after which animals were rewarded with approximately 3 µl of water for contacting the correct lickport. Lickport contacts before the response epoch resulted in the current task epoch restarting, ensuring that they could not progress to the next task epoch until they had stopped licking for the specified length of the current epoch. If the animal did not respond within 3 s of the go cue, this was considered an ‘ignore’ trial, although responses were typically registered within 300 ms of the go cue.\\n    20→\\n    21→Mice used for the two-context task (Figs. 1, 2, 4 and 8 and Extended Data Figs. 1–3 and 9) were introduced to the WC context after they were fully trained on the DR context and at least 2 d before the first electrophysiology recording session. A behavioral session began with approximately 100 DR trials and was then followed by alternating blocks of WC and DR trials. Each interleaved block was 10–25 trials, with no fixed block duration. All sessions started with DR trials. Pilot sessions beginning with WC trials had to be terminated early due to a high ‘ignore’ rate, likely due to the mouse becoming sated early in the session. In a WC trial, all auditory cues were omitted, and an approximately 3-µl water reward was presented randomly from either lickport. Trials in which the animal contacted the lickport before the reward (‘early lick’) were omitted from analyses. ITIs were randomly drawn from an exponential distribution with mean 1.5 s. There were no explicit cues during the ITI to indicate to the animal which context block it was in.\\n    22→\\n    23→For the randomized delay task (Fig. 3g,h,i), mice were first fully trained on the fixed delay DR task (delay duration of 0.9 s). The delay epoch length was then randomized; the duration for each trial was randomly selected from six possible values (0.3 s, 0.6 s, 1.2 s, 1.8 s, 2.4 s and 3.6 s). The probability of each delay duration being selected was assigned such that it resembled a probability density function of an exponential distribution with τ = 0.9 s, as in ref. 44. Animals were trained on this version of the task until they became experts (>70% accuracy and <20% early lick rate).\\n    24→\\n    25→Videography analysis\\n    26→\\n    27→High-speed video was captured (400-Hz frame rate) from two cameras (FLIR, Blackfly monochrome camera, BFS-U3-16S2M-CS). One provided a side view of the mouse, and the other provided a bottom view. We tracked the movements of specific body features using DeepLabCut (Figs. 1, 3 and 4). The tongue, jaw and nose were tracked using both cameras, whereas the paws were tracked using only the bottom view. Position and velocity of each tracked feature was calculated from each camera. The x and y position of each kinematic feature was extracted from the output of DeepLabCut. Missing values were filled in with the nearest available value for all features, except for the tongue. The velocity of each feature was then calculated as the first-order derivative of the position vector. Tongue angle and length were found using the bottom camera. Tongue angle was defined as the angle between the vector pointing from the jaw to the tip of the tongue and the vector defining the direction the mouse was facing. Tongue length was calculated as the Euclidean distance from the jaw to the tip of the tongue.\\n    28→\\n    29→Motion energy\\n    30→\\n    31→The motion energy for a given frame and pixel was defined as the absolute value of the difference between the median value of the pixel across the next five frames (12.5 ms) and the median value of the pixel across the previous five frames (12.5 ms). Motion energy for each frame was then converted to a single value by taking the 99th percentile (~700 pixels) of motion energy values across the frame. Motion energy calculated in this manner was high during overt movements over small regions of pixel space, such as during whisking, while remaining relatively low during passive respiration that corresponded to subtle motion across the animal’s body. A threshold above which an animal was classed as moving was defined on a per-session basis manually. Motion energy distributions, per session, were bimodal, showing a large peak with little variance at low motion energy values and a second, smaller peak with high variance at large values. The threshold was set as the motion energy value separating these two modes. We found that this method of setting the threshold captured both short-duration and long-duration movements. Alternative methods, such as defining a baseline period of no movement against which to compare, were less successful due to the variability in timing of the movements across trials.\\n    32→\\n    33→Photoinactivation experiments\\n    34→\\n    35→Optogenetic photoinactivation was deployed on approximately 30% of trials selected at random. The beam (2-mm diameter) was centered around the following locations: ALM (AP 2.5 mm, ML 1.5 mm), tjM1 (AP 1.75 mm, ML 2.25 mm) and motor cortex (that is, ALM and tjM1; AP 2.25 mm, ML 1.85 mm). All sessions used for behavioral analysis had at least 40 correct DR trials for each direction (left or right) and 20 correct WC trials for each direction, excluding early lick and ignore trials, which were omitted from all analyses. To assess the impact of ALM photoinactivation on movement initiation, we first calculated the percent of trials with a correct lick within 600 ms of the go cue/water drop (Fig. 1c). A unit was considered a well-isolated single unit based on manual inspection of its inter-spike interval (ISI) histogram, separation from other units and its stationarity across the session. Recording sessions were included for analysis only if they had at least 10 units (see Extended Data Fig. 2 for a distribution of neuron counts across sessions). Selective units were those with significantly different spike counts (P < 0.05) during a given epoch. Context-selective units were defined in a two-step process to ensure that we were not conflating context selectivity with slow changes in animal engagement/motivation over each session. First, 40 trials each were subsampled for DR and WC trials, and spike counts were compared (P < 0.05, rank-sum test) during the ITI (the 300 ms preceding the sample tone onset) when the animal received no external cues to indicate which context it was in. Because sessions always began with a DR block and often ended with a WC block, it is possible that differences in firing rates across contexts defined in this way could be representing time within the session. To account for this, for each unit identified in the first step, we calculated the difference in spike rate for each pair of DR and WC blocks (for example, a session with five blocks, DR–WC–DR–WC–DR, would have nPairs = 4 adjacent, overlapping block pairs) and included units as context selective only if their preferred context (context with a higher spike rate) was the same for at least nPairs − 1 of the block pairs.\\n    57→\\n    58→Selectivity in the neural population (Extended Data Fig. 4c) was calculated as the difference in spike rate on preferred − non-preferred trials in choice-selective units, with preferred trials referring to the trial type with a higher spike rate for each unit.\\n    59→\\n\\n[metadata] {\\\"type\\\": \\\"text\\\", \\\"file\\\": {\\\"filePath\\\": \\\"/app/methods.txt\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"Task-switching behavioral paradigm\\\\n\\\\nWe designed a behavioral paradigm associated with multiple cognitive processes. In this paradigm, head-fixed mice performed two directional licking tasks that alternated block-wise within each behavioral session. These tasks varied in their cognitive demands but required the same instructed motor output.\\\\n\\\\nThis paradigm included an established delayed-response (DR) task in which motor planning is temporally dissociated from movement execution (Fig. 1a). In the DR task, an auditory stimulus indicated the location of a reward. After a brief delay epoch with no auditory stimuli, a separate auditory ‘go cue’ instructed the mouse to move. If the mouse performed a directional tongue movement to the correct target, a water reward was delivered. In separate blocks of trials, mice performed a water-cued (WC) task in which all auditory stimuli were omitted. Instead, a drop of water was presented at a random point in time at a randomly selected reward port. Animals consumed water upon its presentation. Mice received no explicit cues signaling DR and WC blocks. The DR task required a perceptual decision that guides the planning of a subsequent motor action. In the WC task, uncertainty in the timing and location of reward prevented formation of a motor plan before reward presentation, and, instead, mice detected reward availability using olfactory and/or vibrissal cues. This structure required animals to maintain an internal representation of the current block identity (context) to maintain high task performance.\\\\n\\\\nWe examined uninstructed movements in this behavioral paradigm using high-speed video. We tracked movement of the tongue, jaw, nose and paws and calculated instantaneous motion energy to quantify movement in a feature-agnostic manner (Fig. 1d–f). We found that mice performed uninstructed movements that varied in their identity and timing across both trials and contexts (Fig. 1e and Supplementary Movie 1).\\\\n\\\\nTo assess cortical involvement in instructed movements (directional licking) in both behavioral tasks, we used optogenetic photoinactivation to inhibit the ALM and tjM1 at the go cue (DR) or water presentation (WC) bilaterally in VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice (10 sessions, four mice). Simultaneous photoinactivation of both regions at the go cue (DR task) or water drop (WC task) impaired the initiation of movement in both contexts (Fig. 1b,c; all DR trials: 41 ± 20% reduction, mean ± s.d., P = 1 × 10−4; all WC trials: 15 ± 20%, P = 0.04; and Extended Data Fig. 1c,d). To assess cortical involvement in the expression of uninstructed movements, and whether these movements might be controlled by ALM or tjM1 preferentially, we bilaterally silenced the ALM or tjM1 individually during the delay epoch of DR trials (ALM: 15 sessions, tjM1: nine sessions, four mice). Uninstructed movements were suppressed by photoinactivation of either area (Extended Data Fig. 1b; ALM: 53 ± 31% reduction, mean ± s.d., P = 3 × 10−4; tjM1: 62 ± 24% reduction, P = 2 × 10−3, paired t-test) and more strongly suppressed by concurrent photoinactivation of both areas (Fig. 1g,h; 29 sessions, four mice; 73 ± 35% reduction, mean ± s.d., P = 7 × 10−9, paired t-test), similar to previous observations21 (but see ref. 34). In the DR task, delay photoinactivation of both areas led to a significant decrease in overall performance (Fig. 1i; 22% ± 14% reduction, mean ± s.d., P = 2 × 10−6 paired t-test; Extended Data Fig. 1b) as expected from the disruption of choice/planning dynamics, often leading to animals responding consistently to a preferred side rather than in a manner commensurate with the sensory cue. These results indicate that both the ALM and tjM1 are involved in the generation of uninstructed movements and the planning and execution of instructed directional tongue movements in the two-context paradigm.\\\\n\\\\nNeural dynamics related to task variables\\\\n\\\\nWhile movement-related and task-related information is encoded in both the ALM and tjM1 in the DR task and other directional licking tasks33, task variables are more strongly represented in the ALM33,36, and so we focused our subsequent analyses there. We recorded activity extracellularly in the ALM with high-density silicon probes during the two-context paradigm to track dynamics associated with planning, context and the execution of movements (Fig. 2; two-context paradigm: 12 sessions, six mice, 522 units, including 214 well-isolated single units; an additional three mice were trained only on the DR task: 25 sessions, nine mice, 1,651 units, including 483 well-isolated single units; see Extended Data Fig. 2a for per-session statistics). In the DR task, we found that choice selectivity (right versus left DR trials) was widespread across all task epochs as expected (sample: 36%; delay: 42%; response: 58% of 483 single units; 25 sessions, nine mice). Individual units showed a variety of activity patterns across trial types, including delay epoch preparatory activity, which has often been taken to be a neural signature of motor planning32,37 (Fig. 2b, left). Individual units were also selective for behavioral context during all task epochs, including during the inter-trial interval (ITI) (39% of single units, 12 sessions, six mice, 214 single units), suggesting persistent coding of context (Fig. 2b, right).\\\\n\\\\nMethods\\\\n\\\\nMouse behavior\\\\n\\\\nBehavioral training was conducted using custom scripts written for Bpod r0.5 (https://www.sanworks.io/shop/products.php?productFamily=bpod). All mice used in experiments were first trained on the DR task with a fixed delay epoch until they reached at least 70% accuracy. At the beginning of each trial, one of two auditory tones lasting 1.3 s was played; the tone indicating a ‘right’ trial was white noise, and the tone indicating a ‘left’ trial was a pure tone (8-kHz pulses). The delay epoch (0.9 s for 12 mice, 0.7 s for one mouse and linearly time warped to 0.9 s) started after the completion of the sample tone. After the delay epoch, an auditory go cue was played (swept-frequency cosine (chirp), 10 ms), after which animals were rewarded with approximately 3 µl of water for contacting the correct lickport. Lickport contacts before the response epoch resulted in the current task epoch restarting, ensuring that they could not progress to the next task epoch until they had stopped licking for the specified length of the current epoch. If the animal did not respond within 3 s of the go cue, this was considered an ‘ignore’ trial, although responses were typically registered within 300 ms of the go cue.\\\\n\\\\nMice used for the two-context task (Figs. 1, 2, 4 and 8 and Extended Data Figs. 1–3 and 9) were introduced to the WC context after they were fully trained on the DR context and at least 2 d before the first electrophysiology recording session. A behavioral session began with approximately 100 DR trials and was then followed by alternating blocks of WC and DR trials. Each interleaved block was 10–25 trials, with no fixed block duration. All sessions started with DR trials. Pilot sessions beginning with WC trials had to be terminated early due to a high ‘ignore’ rate, likely due to the mouse becoming sated early in the session. In a WC trial, all auditory cues were omitted, and an approximately 3-µl water reward was presented randomly from either lickport. Trials in which the animal contacted the lickport before the reward (‘early lick’) were omitted from analyses. ITIs were randomly drawn from an exponential distribution with mean 1.5 s. There were no explicit cues during the ITI to indicate to the animal which context block it was in.\\\\n\\\\nFor the randomized delay task (Fig. 3g,h,i), mice were first fully trained on the fixed delay DR task (delay duration of 0.9 s). The delay epoch length was then randomized; the duration for each trial was randomly selected from six possible values (0.3 s, 0.6 s, 1.2 s, 1.8 s, 2.4 s and 3.6 s). The probability of each delay duration being selected was assigned such that it resembled a probability density function of an exponential distribution with τ = 0.9 s, as in ref. 44. Animals were trained on this version of the task until they became experts (>70% accuracy and <20% early lick rate).\\\\n\\\\nVideography analysis\\\\n\\\\nHigh-speed video was captured (400-Hz frame rate) from two cameras (FLIR, Blackfly monochrome camera, BFS-U3-16S2M-CS). One provided a side view of the mouse, and the other provided a bottom view. We tracked the movements of specific body features using DeepLabCut (Figs. 1, 3 and 4). The tongue, jaw and nose were tracked using both cameras, whereas the paws were tracked using only the bottom view. Position and velocity of each tracked feature was calculated from each camera. The x and y position of each kinematic feature was extracted from the output of DeepLabCut. Missing values were filled in with the nearest available value for all features, except for the tongue. The velocity of each feature was then calculated as the first-order derivative of the position vector. Tongue angle and length were found using the bottom camera. Tongue angle was defined as the angle between the vector pointing from the jaw to the tip of the tongue and the vector defining the direction the mouse was facing. Tongue length was calculated as the Euclidean distance from the jaw to the tip of the tongue.\\\\n\\\\nMotion energy\\\\n\\\\nThe motion energy for a given frame and pixel was defined as the absolute value of the difference between the median value of the pixel across the next five frames (12.5 ms) and the median value of the pixel across the previous five frames (12.5 ms). Motion energy for each frame was then converted to a single value by taking the 99th percentile (~700 pixels) of motion energy values across the frame. Motion energy calculated in this manner was high during overt movements over small regions of pixel space, such as during whisking, while remaining relatively low during passive respiration that corresponded to subtle motion across the animal’s body.
